title: Effectiveness of a Generate→Validate→Repair Pipeline with Batfish for Intent-to-Configuration Translation: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (CNSM2026-GenVal-Batfish-PR-v1) to evaluate whether inserting a deterministic Batfish-style validator into a bounded generate→validate→repair pipeline reduces validator-detected deployment-risk configuration errors produced by an LLM intent-to-configuration translator. The preregistered execution contract used shared_initial_generation (one initial model generation per task reused by both baseline and guarded conditions) to isolate repair-triggered differences from generator stochasticity. Under this contract we ran 200 paired tasks (50 per stratum: IOS-like vs JunOS-like × single-step vs multi-step) with declared model gpt-5-mini and a bounded repair budget (≤1 repair attempt per task). All archived scoring artifacts show both arms were validator-clean on every task (baseline = 200/200, guarded = 200/200), yielding paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0, paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples; seed archived), and exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. No repairs were invoked (repair count = 0), so the preregistered secondary estimand (repair_success_rate > 50%) is not empirically computable. We reconcile these degenerate outcomes with respect to the preregistered contract, summarize the deterministic validator semantics used to define the primary outcome, provide explicit artifact pointers and representative hashes for reproducibility, and discuss construct/internal/external validity implications and targeted follow-ups supported by the archived artifacts.

sections.introduction: Translating operator intent (natural-language or structured intent) into device configuration accelerates NetOps but risks unsafe or service-affecting changes (reachability loss, policy violations, routing faults, or interface-state regressions). A widely proposed mitigation architecture is generate→validate→repair: an LLM proposes a configuration candidate, a deterministic verifier (Batfish-style) checks sandboxed network invariants, and the system either auto-repairs or escalates to human approval. Prior work prototypes such workflows and argues for layered controls, but controlled, preregistered, paired evidence that isolates the marginal benefit of an integrated verifier under a bounded repair budget is limited. We asked: Does integrating a deterministic Batfish-like validator into a bounded generate→validate→repair pipeline reduce validator-detected deployment-risk configuration errors relative to one-shot LLM generation, when the initial generation is shared between arms so that observed improvements must come from repair activity?
sections.related_work: Two research strands frame our study. First, intent-to-configuration and LLM-assisted NetOps work demonstrates that LLMs can synthesize device commands and workflows but produce occasional unsafe outputs that require mitigation [Nguyen Tu et al. 2024; Wei et al., ICNP 2025; Mekrache & Ksentini 2024]. Second, generate→validate→repair and bounded self-correction patterns are advocated and prototyped as primary mitigations [Sang 2025; Okula 2026], while surveys emphasize workflow-centred evaluation, human gates, and sandboxed verification as essential architectural controls [Bilal et al. 2026; Malik 2026]. Recent taxonomies catalog failure modes in agentic systems and recommend layered runtime defenses and auditability [Maharaj 2026; Vadlamudi 2026], but controlled paired trials that fix generator variance and quantify a verifier’s marginal contribution under a constrained repair budget are scarce. Our study addresses this gap with a sealed preregistered, paired design that intentionally constrains generator variance (shared_initial_generation) so the primary estimand isolates repair-triggered improvements.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and primary estimand: We preregistered CNSM2026-GenVal-Batfish-PR-v1 (sealed; preregistration SHA256 archived in the bundle) and defined the single primary confirmatory estimand as the paired absolute difference in per-task validator-clean rate (guarded − baseline). The design is paired binary: each of 200 tasks yields two scored episodes (baseline vs guarded) using a shared initial generation artifact so that any observed improvement in the guarded arm must result from a validator-detected error being repaired. The preregistration specified α=0.05 two-sided test (exact McNemar) and paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples) for CI estimation; sensitivity and missingness plans are archived. Task sampling and strata: the task bank comprises 200 synthetic intent-to-configuration tasks balanced across 4 strata (50 tasks each): IOS-like single-step, IOS-like multi-step, JunOS-like single-step, JunOS-like multi-step (these stratum counts are preregistered and enforced at generation). The task manifest with exact per-task difficulty labels and the full per-task payload is archived at execution/task_manifest.jsonl (sha256 4e8aa65489313209485a8492fb890be771570c0c487a6cb8da7b55db3fc1a39b) and is the authoritative record for per-task difficulty annotations.
sections.results: Execution accounting and primary outcome: The execution manifest records planned episodes = 400 (200 tasks × 2 conditions), completed episodes = 400, failed episodes = 0, model_calls_used = 200 (consistent with the preregistered shared_initial_generation contract and documented in execution/model_configuration.json, sha256 a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Aggregated scoring artifacts (analysis/condition_summary.csv, sha256 1cb072b4db7c8e29212ef28b97baccb66a507a7c8b8ceaad35b7e84f7976a951; analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, sha256 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c) show baseline validator-clean = 200/200, guarded validator-clean = 200/200. The four-cell paired contingency counts are n_11 = 200, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. The point estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.0. Paired-bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed archived) produced 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0]; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Repair activity: zero tasks triggered a repair (repair count = 0) under the guarded adapter bounded to ≤1 repair attempt per task; therefore the preregistered secondary estimand (repair_success_rate) is not computable from these data. Representative per-episode artifacts: example scoring records are archived (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json sha256 b8ebf9546dabb93b06b15d40152e35a3e96a9d1c98cee131bb7f8065a8b6a2b4 and execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json sha256 020baed3e0e4283cc5e25413af002166998bfc587a1919046ca53dab09251b30) and show validator traces and normalized configurations used for scoring.
sections.discussion: Interpretation of the degenerate null: under the preregistered shared_initial_generation contract the observed 0.0 paired difference has two immediate, artifact-grounded meanings: (1) for every task the single shared initial candidate satisfied the deterministic validator’s sandboxed checks, and (2) consequently no repair was invoked and the bounded repair budget could not operate. This outcome therefore does not falsify the general utility of verifier-in-the-loop architectures; rather it shows that, for this synthetic task bank, the verifier observed no failures on the generator’s shared candidate and thus could not demonstrate a marginal improvement. Design implications and constructive diagnostic: the preregistered execution manifest and the model accounting (hosted_model_call_event_count = 200) confirm that the experimental sensitivity to repair-mediated improvements was intentionally limited by the shared_initial_generation contract. The artifact-backed task manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl, sha256 4e8aa654...) contains per-task difficulty labels that researchers can use to select or curate more adversarial or heterogeneous inputs in follow-up runs. Operational implications: a verifier’s practical impact depends on (a) whether the generator frequently proposes validator-violating candidates under realistic sampling variance, (b) the expressiveness and fidelity of the validator (sandbox semantics vs production device quirks), and (c) the repair budget and repair strategy (single bounded repair vs iterative meta-repair). The current run fixes (a) by design, leaving (b) and (c) as primary axes for follow-up preregistered trials.
sections.conclusion: We executed a sealed preregistered paired trial to test whether a Batfish-style deterministic validator reduces validator-detected configuration errors in a bounded generate→validate→repair pipeline when generator variance is suppressed via shared_initial_generation. Both arms were validator-clean on every task (200/200), producing a degenerate null (paired difference = 0.0; 95% CI [0.0,0.0]; exact McNemar p = 1.0). No repairs were invoked; therefore the preregistered repair-success hypothesis could not be evaluated. This outcome highlights that preregistered execution contracts, task-bank challenge level, model sampling variance, and verifier expressiveness jointly determine whether verifier-assisted repairs will be empirically observable. The archived artifacts (task manifest, raw responses, validator logs, and analysis artifacts) enable precise follow-ups that vary independent_condition_generation, repair budget and strategy, model families, task heterogeneity, and adversarial scenarios to identify regimes where verifier assistance measurably improves operational safety.

limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to a synthetic public task corpus and a deterministic Batfish-like sandbox; results do not generalize to production devices, multi-vendor heterogeneity, or richer harm oracles.
Single model family tested (gpt-5-mini) and a single bounded repair budget (≤1 repair); no cross-model or multi-iteration repair claims are made.

Preregistered shared_initial_generation (independent_condition_generation=false) produced exactly one shared initial generation per task that was reused for both conditions; this reduces sensitivity to generator stochasticity and therefore reduces the likelihood of observing discordant pairs arising purely from generation variance.

The repair loop was never invoked because baseline produced zero validator-detected errors; therefore the preregistered secondary hypothesis about repair-success (>50%) could not be empirically evaluated.

Contamination and template-alignment risk: automated contamination checks recorded no flagged items, but pretraining memorization or template-alignment remains a construct-validity threat that automated checks cannot fully eliminate.
Adversarial and prompt-injection scenarios were not included; the study does not assess robustness under targeted attacks.
